Mostly good advice here.  However, concerning index funds versus mutual funds, they weren't very helpful.  They said "56% of mutual funds beat their comparative index over a 12 month period."  Even if this were true (which most years it isn't), over a 15 year period, 82% of mutual funds DO NOT beat their comparative index.  Comparing all of them to the SP500 (instead of different indexes), the number climbs to about 90%.  The problem is the ones that beat the indexes CHANGE every year, and no one can predict which ones will beat each year.  People don't invest for 1 year, but over many.  Indexes are far safer a bet and will be 90% over the long all.  This also, doesn't even consider the greater fees that are usually involved with non-index mutual funds versus index funds.  Index ETFs and mutual funds have lower fees than almost anything else because they don't require active management.  Most everyone who is not an extremely informed, active investor (or who is paying a skilled professional investor they trust), should choose index funds over other mutual funds. This is common knowledge.
